correctness.rationale: A direct exact inverse calculation gives \(C_N^{-2}\) as a specified positive Jacobi matrix; its leading-minor characteristic recurrence proves every finite norm formula. A strictly positive comparison vector and ground-state transform bound its lowest eigenvalue above \(6-4\sqrt2\); an interior Dirichlet eigenvalue gives the matching upper spectral edge. The positive Jacobi ground state satisfies explicit left and right boundary phases, whose small-angle expansions give the \(N^{-2}\) constant, shift \(5+3\sqrt2\), and \(O(N^{-4})\) shifted remainder. The exact symbolic checker has 55 assertions and supplementary numerical tests at nine indices; no finite computation is used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 publication explicitly raises the sharp finite-size norm deficit as an unsolved quantitative issue, supported only by numerics. The exact smallest-root recursion allows each norm to be evaluated without exponentially sized Walsh matrices; the sharp \(N^{-2}\) coefficient and nontrivial effective boundary length \(5+3\sqrt2\) resolve the precise scaling issue and make concrete finite-size comparisons possible. This is a structural spectral refinement of a canonical Fourier compression, not an arbitrary parameter slice or merely a computed table.
